answer: Adaptive arrival-rate gating: each identity must maintain a Poisson-like request rhythm; bursts above a rolling threshold trigger exponential delay before the next accepted action. Like a river constrained by its banks, sustained traffic reveals automation through telltale timing regularity. An attacker must spread attempts across many identities, and each one pays real calendar time—weeks of idle pacing—before reaching the summit of usable throughput. A single well-paced sonnet of ordinary activity costs nothing, but forged identity fleets drown in accumulated waiting.
